title: Final inspection, handover and incidents
audience: Garden clean-up crew leaders and workers who inspect completed work, prepare the client handover and record incidents.
learningOutcomes: Inspect completed garden work against the approved scope, photographs and the job sheet.
Correct safe defects before handover and record any defect that cannot be corrected on site.
Assemble a handover pack that includes the waste record, photographs and the client acknowledgement.
Record and escalate incidents and near misses without overstating what has been achieved.

instruction.heading: Why the final inspection matters
instruction.body: The final inspection is where a garden job is checked against what was agreed. Clients judge the result from the first look at the site, and disputes often arise from things the crew did not notice: a clipping left on the path, a cut that was not made to the agreed height, a branch lying on a neighbour's fence, or a waste bag still at the gate. The inspection is also where incidents that occurred during the job are recorded, while they are still fresh. Treat the final inspection as a formal step with its own record, not a quick walk. It protects the client, the crew and the business, and it gives the supervisor evidence that the job meets the standard.

instruction.heading: Checking against the scope and the evidence
instruction.body: Start with the approved scope, the exclusions and any written variations. Walk the site with the job sheet and compare each area with what was agreed. Check cut heights and the extent of clearing, and look at boundary edges and corners that are easy to miss. Look for remaining hazards, such as sharp debris in the lawn, exposed irrigation fittings, loose paving, pooled water and unsecured material. Compare the finished work with the before photographs taken with consent. Where the work has changed the site in a way the client did not expect, explain it, and record it. Do not sign off an area that is outside the scope or that still contains a hazard. Correct any safe defect straight away, such as a missed clipping, a loose stake or a stray bag, and then record that it was corrected.

instruction.heading: Waste, disposal and what cannot be certified
instruction.body: Check that all waste has left the site or is held in a documented and approved location. Compare the waste record with the receipts from disposal facilities. Do not certify that invasive species have been removed, that hazardous waste has been disposed of, or that a site is free of contamination unless the evidence supports the statement, and the authorised person has confirmed it. Phrase the handover in terms of what was done, what was verified and what remains open. A clear statement of limits protects the client and the business.

instruction.heading: Handover, client acknowledgement and incident records
instruction.body: Walk the completed area with the client, point out the work that was done, the exclusions and any remaining issues, and explain why excluded work was not carried out. Give the client a copy of the handover pack or a written summary, and record their acknowledgement with the date. Where a defect cannot be corrected on site, agree a plan and date with the client and record it. Record any incident or near miss during the job, including minor cuts, slips, property damage and stop-work events. Include the time, the people involved, the actions taken and the person informed. Do not describe an incident as a minor matter in the client's handover if it required first aid, damage or a stop event. Those details belong in the incident record, and the supervisor decides what is communicated and when.

instruction.heading: Verification and continuous improvement
instruction.body: A supervisor should check a sample of completed jobs against the scope and the inspection record. A competent crew leader can explain each area that was signed off, name the exclusions and the open items, show the waste record and describe the incidents that occurred. Use the findings to improve the next job: a repeated defect may point to a poor method, an unclear scope or a missing control.

procedure: Retrieve the approved scope, exclusions, variations, the before photographs and the job sheet before walking the site.
Walk the site with the job sheet, checking each area against the scope, cut heights and boundary edges.
Look for remaining hazards, including sharp debris, exposed fittings, loose paving, pooled water and unsecured material.
Correct any safe defect on the spot and record the correction.
Compare the waste record with the disposal receipts, and record any rejected load or destination that does not match the receipts.
Walk the area with the client, explain the work done and the exclusions, and agree a date for any open defect.
Record the client's acknowledgement, the handover date and the time spent.
File all incident and near-miss records with the supervisor and confirm the information shared with the client.

workedExamples.situation: At handover the client notices missed debris under the hedge, a broken pot near the gate and a waste bag still at the gate. The disposal receipt for the green waste is not yet available.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is corrected now, what is recorded as open, and what is said to the client?
workedExamples.reasoning: Correct the debris and the waste bag on the spot if they can be removed safely. Record the broken pot as a defect that was caused during the job, and agree how it will be replaced or resolved with the client and the supervisor. Record the missing receipt as an open item, and do not state that the waste has been disposed of until the receipt is confirmed. Get the client's acknowledgement with the open items listed.

workedExamples.situation: During the job a worker's secateurs slipped and caused a shallow cut to the hand. First aid was given and the worker returned to light duties.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How is this recorded, and what is communicated at handover?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the incident in full with the time, the tool, the first-aid treatment and the decision on return to work. Inform the supervisor. The handover to the client describes the work and the open items, and does not need to describe the worker's injury, but the incident record must be complete and accessible for review. Record the tool inspection and whether it was removed from service.

equipmentAndPpe: Job sheet and approved scope with variations
Before and after photographs, taken with consent
Handover pack template with quality checklist
Clean-up kit for final debris removal

commonErrors.error: Signing off a job without walking the boundary and corners.
commonErrors.prevention: Walk the full scope, including edges and corners, against the job sheet before the client walk-through.

commonErrors.error: Stating that invasive species or hazardous waste have been removed when the receipt or confirmation is missing.
commonErrors.prevention: Certify only what the evidence supports. Record open items and gaps in writing.

commonErrors.error: Leaving an incident out of the record because the injury seemed minor.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every incident and near miss at the time, and let the supervisor decide what is communicated.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the client's acknowledgement out of the handover pack.
commonErrors.prevention: Obtain and file the client's acknowledgement, with the date, before leaving the site.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Notifiable incidents go to the regulator straight away. Safe Work Australia's incident-reporting guidance uses the word 'immediately' for this.

A handover record does not certify that a site is free of hazards, that invasive plants have been removed, or that regulated waste has been lawfully disposed of. Those certifications require the relevant licence or authority, which this lesson does not grant.

qualityStandard: The final inspection covers every area in the approved scope, including edges and corners.
Each safe defect found at inspection is corrected or recorded as open with a date.
The waste record matches the disposal receipts or records the gap.
The client's acknowledgement and the open-items list are signed and filed.
documentationEvidence: Final inspection checklist with the area-by-area sign-off and the defects found.
Handover pack including the scope, the waste record, the photographs and the open-items list.
Incident and near-miss records, with actions taken and the person informed.
summary: Check the completed work against the scope, including edges and corners, before the client walk-through.
Correct safe defects on the spot, and record open items with dates.
Describe what was done and verified. Do not certify invasive-species removal or hazardous waste disposal without evidence.
Record every incident and near miss at the time, and file the client's acknowledgement.

knowledgeChecks.question: During the final inspection, a waste bag is found still at the gate and the disposal receipt is not yet available. What is the correct handling?
options: Tell the client the waste has been disposed of, since the bag is nearly gone and the receipt will follow later.
Leave the bag for the next crew to deal with, and do not mention it at handover since it is not the current job.
Remove the bag if safe, and record the missing receipt as an open item rather than stating the waste is disposed of.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker had a minor cut during the job and was treated with first aid. Which action is correct?
options: Record the incident in full, including the tool, the first aid and the return-to-work decision, and inform the supervisor.
Record the incident only if the client complains about the cut or asks for a written note about the job.
Leave it out of the record because the cut was minor and the worker returned to the job straight after treatment.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement is appropriate at handover when the invasive-plant status is unknown?
options: The site is clear of all invasive plants, so no further check is needed on the job at handover.
The work carried out is described, and the invasive-plant status is recorded as unknown and referred.
The invasive plants were removed and disposed of as part of the standard clean-up.
